entry.title: About and license
entry.summary: Attribution and license (CC-BY-SA-4.0) for the Rhetoric showcase — the public-domain Freese/Perseus source and the Dejongh revamp.
entry.content:
The Rhetoric section is a real, worked example: a conversion of Aristotle’s Rhetoric into doc-kitty pages, used to show a full Markua-authored work rendering natively. It is not a copy of the book itself — it is a docsite conversion of one existing translation, restructured, lightly edited for the modern reader, and annotated with editor’s notes.

License

This section is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC-BY-SA-4.0).

This is separate from doc-kitty’s own MIT code license. The MIT license covers the doc-kitty toolkit (the templates, components, and build pipeline); CC-BY-SA-4.0 covers the content of this Rhetoric section specifically — the converted text, editor’s notes, and glossary on these pages. Reusing code from this repository is governed by the project’s MIT license; reusing the prose on these pages is governed by CC-BY-SA-4.0 and requires attribution plus share-alike redistribution of any derivative.

Attribution

This section is a derivative work with two layers of attribution:

  • Source translation: the underlying text is J.H. Freese’s 1926 English translation of Aristotle’s Rhetoric, which is in the public domain. Freese’s translation was published by the Perseus Project — the Perseus Digital Library maintained by the Department of Classical Studies at Tufts University — and incorporates translation notes from E. M. Cope (1877) and W. D. Ross (1959). Neither Freese’s translation nor the Perseus Project take any credit for, or claim any ownership of, this derivative conversion.
  • This revamp: the restructuring into a modern, navigable docsite — chapter titles, editor’s notes, the glossary, and cross-reference conversion — is © Stijn Dejongh, 2024, licensed under CC-BY-SA-4.0 to keep the spirit of the original Perseus publication (which was itself licensed CC-BY-SA-3.0).

The Perseus Project

The Perseus Project — also known as the Perseus Hopper — is a long-running online digital library curated by the Department of Classical Studies at Tufts University. As an open source project, it has had many contributors since its founding in 1987. It is named after the Greek hero Perseus, the mythical slayer of monsters and legendary founder of Mycenae.

Tufts University aims to provide a comprehensive catalogue of texts from the ancient world so modern audiences can access them freely, and licenses its own work accordingly to enable that free sharing of knowledge.

See the Introduction for more on how this conversion came about, and the bibliography record for the full source citation.
